ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is an isobar distribution map of the Central Asia region, marking rivers such as the Ural River, the Syr Darya, and the Amu Darya, as well as inland water bodies. The Amu Darya is located from the lower right to the middle-lower part of the figure, and the lower reaches of the river point toward the Aral Sea, an inland water body slightly below the middle of the figure. Reasoning: The question asks what landform will form at the mouth of the Amu Darya. When a river enters a lake or ocean, its flow speed decreases, its ability to transport sediment weakens, and sediment deposits near the river mouth, usually forming a delta. The lower reaches of the Amu Darya flow into the Aral Sea, so a delta will form at its river mouth.
